F1 · HARBOR MILE — B1 gives the bones, D2 gives the light. The section rail survives as calm wayfinding, but it is lit like a marquee: gold bulb on the chapter you are in.

TRADEOFF: the most legible of the three and the least surprising — it reads as B1 with better lighting rather than as a new thing.

F2 · THE LIT MILE — D2 gives the bones. You walk one continuous mile of signage; B1 is grafted in at THE PROOF as the window wall, where every lit window is a session logged tonight.

TRADEOFF: no rail means no map — a visitor cannot see how long the page is, and the window wall goes dark at launch with no user data.

F3 · NIGHT HARBOR — neither parent wins; the page TRANSFORMS. It opens on open water, the reflections harden into wet pavement, and the far windows resolve into neon. One move, no cut.

TRADEOFF: the boldest and the most fragile — the whole idea only lands if the art in all three beats is regraded to match, and it is the hardest to keep coherent on mobile.

THREE FUSIONS OF B1 + D2 — 2026-08-20

Sean picked B1 (Harbor Lights) and D2 (Vegas Mile), then asked for them combined into one final page. These are three ways to combine them, differing on ONE axis: which parent supplies the ARCHITECTURE and which supplies the LIGHT.

SHARED BY ALL THREE (do not vary):
• Sean's real header, lifted BYTE-IDENTICALLY from the approved B1 source — not retyped
• hero = a real frame from his own Swans.mp4, badged as a swappable slot
• 2 movie areas per board for MiniMax H3 films
• parallax depth stages between chapters, not only in the hero
• copy verbatim from copy-pack.json; gold tags mark new lines needing approval
• real harvested plates + the real low-poly crystalline mark

Pick one, or name the graft (e.g. "F2's window wall inside F1").
